modules.topic: Rate-Based Rules  +  Bot Control  +  Rule Tuning  +  DDoS & Central Governance
modules.module_group: Module 3 — Deep Dive: AWS WAF, DDoS & Edge Security
subtopics: Count-mode observation before rule promotion
Labelled benign and malicious request fixtures
Rule-match evidence and benign false positives
Rate-based rule aggregation and test limits
Promotion and rollback criteria
Bot Control, Shield and central policy scope as demonstrations
learning_objectives: Trace each fixture request to observed WAF rule evidence
Reduce the seeded false positive while retaining matches for both suspicious fixtures
Explain why a small passing fixture is insufficient evidence for production promotion
modules.lab: Use a prepared training Web ACL in Count mode. Replay ten labelled requests containing eight benign cases and two suspicious cases against the isolated lab application. Capture the matched rule for each request, investigate the seeded benign false positive and adjust the candidate rule. Demonstrate rate-rule behaviour separately using a bounded trainer-controlled request run.
modules.deliverable: Ten-row request/result matrix, before-and-after rule configuration, false-positive investigation and promotion/rollback decision
modules.assessment: All ten request IDs have traceable results. Both suspicious fixtures still match the intended rule; none of the eight benign fixtures matches it after tuning. Record remaining coverage limits and a rollback condition. Count mode is not reported as having blocked a request.

delivery_steps.activity: Trace Count-mode matches and distinguish matches from blocks
delivery_steps.evidence: Annotated request log

delivery_steps.activity: Run ten cases and investigate the false positive
delivery_steps.evidence: Baseline request/result matrix

delivery_steps.activity: Tune and rerun cases; observe bounded rate-rule demo
delivery_steps.evidence: Comparison matrix and tuning rationale

delivery_steps.activity: Defend promotion criteria and discuss optional central controls
delivery_steps.evidence: Decision with limitations and rollback conditions
